evidence_layer: synthetic memory oracle: the original ARM bytes at 0x19324c / 0x1994dc executed over one staged arena, with identical stubs on both arms; NOT device execution

linked_for_real: CInstance::SetObjectIndex@0x19324c - arm A runs the original bytes (also inside the constructor), arm B runs src/set_object_index.c

covered: F1: no old object (0x19326c) and a live old object (0x193274 RemoveInstance) - and the index is re-read from +0x7c after the call, which an instrumented stub makes observable
F1: objindex -1 is stored as 0 but LOOKED UP as -1; a hash node keyed -1 hits while the field says 0, and objindex 0 with a node keyed 0 hits independently (cases 5..7)
F1: empty bucket, head match, second-node match, chain exhaustion, and a matched node whose value is 0 (cases 1, 10..14)
F1: addToObject true / false / 2 - AddInstance strictly before the field copy, and +0x80 re-read after it (an instrumented AddInstance re-points it, so the copy visibly uses OBJ3)
F1: the six copied fields incl. all three flag bits, bits 3+ ignored, depth as (float)(int) for INT_MAX / 2^24+1 / INT_MIN and sprite handed to SetSpriteIndex
F1: a hit sets +0x64 and tail-calls CollisionMarkDirty; a miss leaves +0x64 alone and calls nothing

F2: every documented field store of the 0x1b0-byte object, alarm[0..11] twice (0 then -1, twelve times each), the three self rings, the create-counter snapshot, the two image 1.0f groups, gravity_direction 270.0f, +0x16c = 2, +0x48 = 1
F2: +0x80 cleared before SetObjectIndex, proven on a stale block that already held an object pointer (case 12)
F2: the instance table - slot -1 with cap 0, a part-full scan, the next_free==cap clamp, two grow paths (4->6 and 2->3 with realloc + zeroed tail) and the slot landing in +0x44
F2: the builtin loop - gate off, count 0, two registrations, the isGlobalBuiltinVar skip (first entry, and both entries)
F2: the base ctor gate writes +0x10/+0x14 and the ctor clears both; the base argument is forwarded verbatim incl. INT_MIN
F2: prefilled 0xa5 blocks and the four slots nobody writes (0x144/0x148/0x178/0x17c) survive
not_covered: CObjectGM::RemoveInstance / AddInstance semantics (stubbed): these arms prove they are called once, in that order, with the right object and instance; the stubs also scribble +0x7c and re-point +0x80 on purpose, which is a probe, not a claim

CInstance::SetSpriteIndex semantics (stubbed): the stub writes +0x8c and nothing else. The real body also resets +0x90 when the sprite does not exist, frees a CSkeletonInstance at +0x88, sets +0x64 and tail-calls CollisionMarkDirty
CollisionMarkDirty semantics (stubbed): log only, so the 0x198/0x19c/0x1a0 dirty list is not exercised here

YYObjectBase::YYObjectBase semantics (stubbed): the write set is the one cards/CInstance_ctor.c documents, and it is a fixture assumption. The ctor overwrites +0x00, +0x44 and +0x48; the leftovers are compared but not attributed

isGlobalBuiltinVar / JS_SetupBuiltinProperty / YYObjectBase::Add semantics (stubbed): the loop shape, the entry stride, the skip decision and the three call arguments are proven, the property machinery is not
YYRealloc semantics (stubbed): the bump allocator and its 0x5b fill / 0xdeadbeef guard are a fixture model, identical on both arms
the negative-capacity table edge (cap < 0) - the original loops for ever there, so it is not a case; see card_deltas
not_applicable: Neither body reads a rodata string or calls a PLT entry except memset in the table-grow path, so there is no error-message contract to compare.
SetObjectIndex has no stack argument and no floating-point input: its whole input domain is (int32 objindex, int32 bool).

findings: F1 re-reads +0x7c from memory after RemoveInstance returns (0x193278) instead of keeping the argument in a register, and it re-reads +0x80 after AddInstance returns (0x19335c) instead of keeping the node value. Both are observable only because the stubs are instrumented, and both are reproduced by the C.

The -1 / 0 asymmetry is real and testable: +0x7c is normalised to 0, the hash key is not. A node keyed -1 is reachable only through objindex == -1 (bucket 7), and objindex 0 reaches a node keyed 0 (bucket 0) - the two requests differ.

A matched node with a NULL value is not a hit: +0x80 becomes 0 and the function returns at 0x1932f4 without touching +0x64 or calling CollisionMarkDirty. The instance keeps its previous sprite, mask, flags and depth.

+0x64, +0x65, +0x66 and +0x67 are four bytes of ONE word: the bbox dirty bit, visible, solid and persistent. Any dump or comparison that reads +0x64 as a word is reading all four at once, which is why the coverage checks use the byte.

The alarm array is written twice: zero first (a loop over +0xf8 + 4*i, 12 times) and then -1 (a second loop over the same range). The first pass is redundant against a fresh block but not against a reused one, which is why the prefilled cases matter.

The constructor clears +0x80 at 0x19964c before calling SetObjectIndex, so the RemoveInstance branch is unreachable from the constructor even on a recycled instance - mutant ctor_object_pointer_not_precleared shows exactly that: with a stale +0x80 the mutant calls RemoveInstance and the original does not.

A table with cap 0 is not "no work": count >= cap holds (0 >= 0), so the grow path runs once with newcap = 0, i.e. YYRealloc(base, 0) and memset(ptr, 0, 0) are both called, cap stays 0, and only then does the scan report slot -1. The call log of that case is the evidence (RA ... 0 / MS ... 0).
Instance-table growth is (3*cap + ((3*cap) >>u 31)) >>a 1, i.e. floor(1.5*cap) for positive cap, and the scan restarts at 0x199770 so the count>=cap test is not repeated for the grown table.

The builtin count is re-read from 0x753108 on every iteration (0x19980c and 0x199850) while the table base is cached in r4 at 0x199800 - a callee that changed the base would not be seen, a callee that changed the count would.
card/byte agreement: every address, opcode, offset and constant in the two cards was re-checked against llvm-objdump; see card_deltas. One prose fix, one open question sharpened.

card_deltas.claim: 71 条 = 70 条指令 + 末 1 字池字 0x193364；+0x7c 先写后归一；查表键用原始 objindex；命中才置 +0x64 并尾调 CollisionMarkDirty
card_deltas.bytes: 70 instructions 0x19324c..0x193360 + 1 pool word 0x193364 = 284 B; the arm reproduces every one of those claims, including the -1 / 0 asymmetry (cases 5..9) and the tail branch (0x19334c is a b, and CollisionMarkDirty runs with LR still the caller of SetObjectIndex)

card_deltas.claim: 字段来源：mask ← obj+0x10，visible ← bit1，solid ← bit0，persistent ← bit2，depth ← (float)(int)obj+0x08，sprite ← SetSpriteIndex(obj+0x04)
card_deltas.bytes: every one reproduced; the flag/bit assignment is pinned by cases 15 and 16 (flags 0x0d / 0xffffffff / 0x00000001) and the int reading of obj+0x08 by the 2^24+1 depth case

card_deltas.claim: 257 条 = 249 条指令 + 8 池字；107 条直接存储 + 2 条循环（各 12 次）= 131 次写；sizeof = 0x1b0；+0x144/+0x148/+0x178/+0x17c 谁都不写
card_deltas.bytes: 249 instructions + 8 pool words = 1028 B, and the annotation census covers all of them; the arm writes 0xa5 into those four slots before the call and they still hold 0xa5 afterwards (coverage f2_untouched_slots_kept)

card_deltas.claim: 基类第 1 实参来自 *(int*)0x544b48；实例表 0x536f0c {base,cap,count,next_free}；count>=cap 时 newcap = cap*3/2，YYRealloc + memset 新段
card_deltas.bytes: GOT cells 0x003edd1c -> 0x00544b48, 0x003edc6c -> 0x00536f0c, and the growth arithmetic (3*cap + (3*cap >>u 31)) >>a 1 is reproduced byte for byte; both grow scenarios are exercised (4->6 and 2->3)

card_deltas.claim: 内建属性表基址 0x75310c，16B 项；count 0x753108
card_deltas.bytes: exactly right, and the distinction matters: the GOT cell 0x003edc40 holds 0x0075310c, and `ldr r4,[r8,r3]` at 0x199800 IS the single dereference that reaches it - the table starts AT 0x0075310c, it is not a pointer stored there. The first draft of this fixture modelled it as a pointer variable and arm A then read the .bss zeros; the trace of 0x19981c settled it (r4 = 0x00753114 on the first iteration, i.e. table+8). count at 0x00753108 is the mirror case: `ldr r7,[r8,r3]` gives the address and `ldr r3,[r7]` reads the integer
card_deltas.verdict: consistent (the card's reading is the one the bytes support)

card_deltas.claim: open: cap<=0 时槽号 -1 仍是唯一"入表失败"分支
card_deltas.bytes: true, but the negative-capacity edge is worse than "slot -1": with cap < 0 the count>=cap test at 0x19976c is true, the grow path computes newcap = (3*cap + carry) >> 1 which is <= cap for every negative cap, and the `b 0x199770` at 0x1998bc skips the test - so the body oscillates between grow and scan for ever. Not exercised as a case (both arms would hang); recorded as a finding instead
card_deltas.verdict: open, sharpened: cap < 0 does not fail, it loops

card_note: No instruction address, opcode, offset or constant in the two cards disagrees with the bytes. One prose-level delta in cards/CInstance_ctor.c about 0x0075310c being the address of the builtin-table pointer variable rather than the table base, and one open question sharpened: a negative instance-table capacity makes the constructor loop for ever.

repeat.note: identical digests inside an arm are the repeatability evidence; the two arms agreeing with each other is the identity gate

tail_call_evidence.note: CollisionMarkDirty is entered with the lr its caller was called with, so 0x19334c is a `b` and the callee's return value is SetObjectIndex's own. The C arm cannot observe lr; its side of the same contract is that CollisionMarkDirty is the last call and the function then returns

heap_model.note: bump allocator over IC_HEAP inside the arena; identical on both arms; the fill is invisible in a correct run by construction and becomes visible when a translation mis-sizes the memset (mutant ctor_memset_len)
